Romney.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Romney calls follow the ground the town sits on: south Branch Potomac River (west of town), Indian Mound and historic core on the valley floor, forested ridges rising east toward Short Mountain. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, woodchucks, striped skunks in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

Spring is denning season here, summer is bat season in the older housing stock, and fall brings a second push as squirrels and rodents look for winter shelter. Romney's homes date from the 1700s onward — stone, brick, and frame houses in the historic core with postwar streets around it. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.
